messages:
jess_cust_acme: Hey folks — we started removing users from the ‘contractors’ group in Okta earlier and they still have access in Redwood. SCIM logs show a bunch of 403 responses from your side. Can someone help? Org: acme-corp, org_id: org_9X7. We need deprovisioning to be immediate.

alex_cs: Hi Jess — sorry for the trouble. Can you paste the SCIM request/response that shows the 403? Also what connector is this (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace)?

jess_cust_acme: Okta. Here’s the excerpt from our syslogs (redacted):

```json
PATCH /Groups/9a3b-... HTTP/1.1
Host: scim.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ****REDACTED****
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "remove",
      "path": "members[value eq \"00u1abcd2\"]"
    }
  ]
}

Response:
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "schemas": [],
  "detail": "insufficient_scope: token missing groups.write scope",
  "status": 403
}
```

alex_cs: Thanks — that matches a token-scope problem. Our SCIM endpoints require group write permissions to accept PATCH ops that change membership. If your SCIM token only had read or users.write scopes, Okta’s PATCH will be rejected with a 403 and deprovisioning won’t apply.

jordan_sa: @jess_cust_acme do you know if anyone rotated the SCIM token recently or if you used the limited-scope token from the old quickstart?

jess_cust_acme: We rotated about a week ago via the Okta UI — the app told us to re-enter a token and we used the one the security team generated. They didn’t tell us which scopes they requested from Redwood.

maria_engineer: Quick diagnostic steps we use: 1) Check the token scopes in Redwood Console -> Settings -> SCIM -> Tokens (if you can view). 2) Reproduce with curl against the /Groups endpoint to see exact error. 3) If PATCH is blocked, a short-term workaround is to configure the IdP to do a full replace (PUT) of the Group or to have the token created with the groups.write scope.

alex_cs: Example curl to test (replace TOKEN and GROUP_ID):

```bash
curl -i -X PATCH https://scim.redwood.ai/Groups/GROUP_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"members[value eq \"USER_OKTA_ID\"]"}]}'
```

If you get 403 with detail pointing at missing groups.write (or scim.groups.write), that confirms the scope issue.

jess_cust_acme: Ok I ran that and got the same 403, detail: "insufficient_scope: missing scim.groups.write". How do we get a token with that scope?

maria_engineer: Two options: (A) In the Redwood Console create a new SCIM token and ensure you check Group management / groups.write (labels differ slightly in the UI). (B) If your security team insists on tokens with minimal scopes, ask them to add just groups.write in addition to users.write. We can also issue a short-lived support token for you while you rotate permanently (I can generate one if you want).

jordan_sa: For Okta specifically, there’s also a provisioning setting: "Push groups and memberships" vs "Only push group membership changes (PATCH)" — if you flip to full group push it will use PUT semantics which may succeed with a users.write token (but less efficient). Not ideal long-term.

jess_cust_acme: Security wanted minimal scopes so they gave us a users.read/users.write token only. I can ask them to add groups.write. Will that immediately unblock things?

alex_cs: Yes, once you replace the token with one that includes groups.write, Okta PATCH requests should return 200 and membership changes will apply. After you rotate, please run the curl test again and we’ll watch the audit logs on our side.

scim-provisioner-bot: [system] New provisioning token used from IP 52.34.12.8 — token has scopes: scim.users.read, scim.users.write (no scim.groups.write)

maria_engineer: Internal note: this case highlights a runtime gap — if we get 403 for PATCH due to missing groups.write we should fallback to a GET+PUT flow (read the current group, apply change, PUT back) instead of leaving deprovision in limbo. Filing an engineering task to implement fallback and a monitoring alert.

alex_cs: Jess — if you can, rotate the token now and paste the first 8 chars of the new token (we’ll verify on our logs, don’t post full token). Once rotated we’ll confirm on our side.

jess_cust_acme: New token rotated. First 8 chars: ab12cd34. I re-ran the curl and got 204 No Content. Okta shows users removed now.

alex_cs: Saw matching successful response in our logs for GROUP_ID at 2028-06-04T16:03:21Z — 204. Deprovisioning events processed and members removed.

jess_cust_acme: Confirmed — access revoked for the users in question. Thanks for the fast help.

maria_engineer: Follow-ups we’ll do: 1) Create an ops ticket to add PATCH->GET+PUT fallback + telemetry (ENG-5487). 2) Add a note to the SCIM docs about required scopes per IdP and the Okta provisioning mode caveat. 3) Add an alert when repeated 403s from a single org occur on Groups endpoints.

jordan_sa: I’ll update the customer-facing KB with the Okta screenshots to avoid future confusion.

alex_cs: Closing the thread — Jess, please re-open if you see anything else. :thumbsup:

jess_cust_acme: Will do. Appreciate it!
